city_center.name: Pike Place Market (Downtown Seattle waterfront)
city_center.landmark: Pike Place Market neon clock + brass pig ('Rachel'), western views to Elliott Bay, Puget Sound, and the Olympic Range
city_center.notes: Pike Place is one of the oldest continuously operated public farmers markets in the US (opened 1907), a nine-acre historic district of one-to-three-story wood and brick structures on steep streets, with 90+ local farmers bringing produce grown within ~100 miles of Seattle. The mid-week 'Produce on Pike' market runs Wednesday evenings June-September. sources: Pike Place Market (en.wikipedia.org); tclf.org Pike Place Public Market Historic District; pikeplacemarket.org (90+ farmers, 100-mile radius; Produce on Pike).

cultural_notes: Pike Place Market is Seattle's civic food landmark: a 1907 public market, protected as a historic district in 1971, still running the 'meet the producer' tradition seven days a week with 90+ farmers sourcing within ~100 miles (source: Pike Place Market, pikeplacemarket.org; en.wikipedia.org)

long-tenured market producers anchor the seasonal calendar -- Alberg Cherry Farms has brought Rainier, Van, Lambert, and Bing cherries for over four decades; Chukar Cherries has operated in the market since 1992 (source: pikeplacemarket.org vendor profiles)
coffee-forward rain-morning culture and a strong Costco-bulk shopping pattern define the breakfast occasion (source: localization-table-seed.json audience/message)
the Chinatown-International District anchors a large Vietnamese, Chinese, Filipino, and pan-Asian food community (source: en.wikipedia.org Chinatown-International District, Seattle)

Washington is the top US apple-producing state, and the Yakima/Wenatchee valleys east of the Cascades supply the market's fall apples and pears (source: general Washington agriculture framing; publicly documented)
the brass pig 'Rachel' and the neon market clock are the market's signature civic icons, a recurring styling anchor (source: historylink.org Pike Place Market)

state-awareness framing: when a shopper's Washington location is noted, both Seattle Costco-bulk creative and Neah Bay frontier-DTC creative are eligible for the same audience -- intentional, so urban folks see frontier representation (source: localization-table-seed.json seattle_awareness / urban_frontier_link)
